scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The letkajenkka originated in Finland in 1963, evolving from the traditional Jenkka folk dance.
Composers Erik Lindström and Rauno Lehtinen were instrumental in popularizing the genre by blending traditional structures with modern instrumentation.
The dance craze spread rapidly across Europe, reaching its height by 1965.

Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance served as a social novelty and a popular craze in the mid-1960s.
It was used for entertainment and group participation rather than ritual or sacred purposes.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Participants form a conga-style line, holding the shoulders or waist of the person in front.
The sequence involves kicking the left foot twice, the right foot twice, followed by a jump forward, a jump backward, and three jumps forward.
Watch for Side Kick, Forward/Backward Jump.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (IDbIYXEsdx0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Conga line or circle.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is based on the Jenkka rhythm, typically in 4/4 time.
It features a mix of traditional folk elements and 1960s pop instrumentation, including electric guitars, bass, drums, and brass sections.
Listen for the Electric guitar, Bass, Drums, Brass.
The pulse is 4/4.
A blend of traditional folk melodies played with modern 1960s pop-rock instrumentation, characterized by a bouncy, skipping rhythm.
